The reason is that I would like to feed a 433MHz transmitter with the (raw) PF data to control my RF receiver equipped PF trains. This is super simple 433 MHz OOK modulation of the raw bits. posts.title: What do you honestly think about LEGO NINJAGO Legends and the future of NINJAGO?
posts.text: Hey everyone! I'm a 17-year-old student from Kazakhstan, and my team is currently working on a project for the Hult Future Leaders Challenge 2026, focused on LEGO NINJAGO Legends and how to make the franchise more appealing to teenagers aged 13–17. I've been a NINJAGO fan since childhood, but personally, I feel like something has changed over the years. I'm curious whether other fans feel the same way. I'd really appreciate your honest opinions on a few questions: What do you think about NINJAGO Legends? Do you find its sets, storytelling, and overall concept interesting? How do you feel about the newer NINJAGO content compared to the original series? Has the franchise improved, declined, or simply changed? If you've stopped watching NINJAGO or buying its sets, what made you lose interest? Do you think LEGO NINJAGO still appeals to teenagers (13–17), or is it mainly targeting younger children and adult collectors? What would make you genuinely excited about NINJAGO again? A new animated series, a darker storyline, a video game, more affordable sets, or something completely different? I'm especially interested in hearing from longtime fans, teenagers, and people who used to love NINJAGO but have moved on. I'm not trying to prove that modern NINJAGO is bad. I want to understand what the community actually thinks, including positive opinions. Your feedback could help us develop a real concept for our competition project. Thank you! I'd love to hear your thoughts.

posts.title: [WIP] Train-Actuated Signals
posts.text: I've been tinkering with an experiment: signals that automatically go from "clear" to "danger" when a train passes. Not owning any PF/PUp components forced me to pursue a purely mechanical solution. Using flex tube as a "trigger," the train wheels push the lever over a rounded detent, raising the signal arm (these are old-fashioned lower-quadrant signals). They still require resetting manually, but I'm happy with them for now. Eventually, I'd like to explore an automatic reset mechanism. Here is the home signal in the "all clear" position. And here is the home signal set to "danger." Here are the signals in action. I know the spacing between them is utterly unrealistic, but I wanted both the distant and home signals to fit within the station module for portability. I hope this will be useful to other train builders!

posts.title: [MOC] Passenger transport shuttle
posts.text: I drew inspiration from the animated series *Star Wars: The Clone Wars*. This is a passenger transport shuttle originating from the planet Coruscant. - 2 seats for pilots. - 12 seats for passengers. - Deployable rear ramp for boarding. - Adjustable, tiltable engines. - 3 landing skids. I aimed for a cohesive aesthetic, characterized by a rounded, organic shape. For the engines—which can be oriented or tilted in any direction—I used reinforced Technic parts: - 2x 47455: Technic ball joint with 2 perpendicular axles (friction-fit) - 79505: Technic articulation disc with a wide axle and 2 rotation points - 80563: Technic articulation disc with a socket for a wide axle and 2 axles Specifications: - Weight: 1686 g - Dimensions: 33.2 cm x 48.5 cm x 14.0 cm - Total parts: 2045 - Total lots: 237 As is my custom: everything is accessible, just as it would be for a child. And for visual appeal, I’ve used AI to enhance the background, adding the planet Coruscant—just to see how well the shuttle fits into that setting. Also on Rebrickable : https://rebrickable.com/mocs/MOC-280900/Horlack/passenger-transport-shuttle/#details

posts.title: The Entombment of an Ultramarine Dreadnough
posts.text: Hey all! I'm mostly a castle builder, but i have another huge liking, as a hobby. I'm a huge Warhammer 40k fan. 10 years ago, when i joined this community, i was at a crossroads. I was started to know more and more about WH40k , but i wasn't really into spend money on armies and painting and learing the rules, how to play. In the other hand, i had a lot of Lego. 10years ago, I decided, i will stick with Lego, but as soon as I'm able, i will build WH40k MOCs and dioramas. And today is the day, i start show you how I imagine the grim darkness of the far future. With Lego Bricks. What's Warhammer 40k? well, i suggest look after in the internet. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The Entombment of an Ultramarine Dreadnough The World of Warhammer 40,000 Warhammer 40,000 is a science-fiction universe set in a dark, distant future, where humanity wages constant war for its survival. Despite technological advancements, religion, superstition, and ancient traditions shape everyday life. The franchise's motto captures this reality: “In the grim darkness of the far future, there is only war.” The Imperium of Man The Imperium spans countless worlds, with its population spread across billions of planets. Humanity must face alien species, internal heresy, and the daemonic horrors emerging from the Immaterium, also known as the Warp. The Space Marines The Adeptus Astartes, commonly known as Space Marines, are genetically and surgically enhanced super-soldiers. Possessing superhuman strength, endurance, and specialised power armour, their purpose is to defeat the Imperium's most dangerous enemies. The Ultramarines – The XIII Legion The Ultramarines were one of the original 18 Space Marine Legions and remain among the best-known and most respected Chapters. They are renowned for their discipline, tactical expertise, and unwavering loyalty to the Imperium. Apothecaries and Techmarines Apothecaries serve as the healers of their Chapters: they treat the wounded and preserve the gene-seed of fallen Battle-Brothers. Techmarines are responsible for maintaining weapons and war machines, having received additional training in the teachings of the Adeptus Mechanicus of Mars. During a Dreadnought's entombment, both the warrior's condition and the life-support systems must be carefully monitored. The Tech-Priests of Mars The Tech-Priests of the Adeptus Mechanicus dedicate their lives to the sacred service of machines. They oversee machinery through rituals and ancient protocols, participating in both the technical procedures and the associated rites during a Dreadnought's entombment. Servo-skulls and Servitors Servo-skulls are floating devices fashioned from the skulls of deceased humans, used for surveillance, data transmission, and various technical tasks. Servitors are lobotomised, cybernetically modified humans employed for physical labour, machine operation, and other duties. During the entombment, both assist the Tech-Priests and Techmarines in their work. I will upload more pictures, just need a little more time

posts.title: Using Claude AI for new ports and translations
posts.text: For free Gemini (or FFG) insists that you can't make a new Atari version of the LEGO Lines/DOS executable, and it listed about 100 reasons why that won't work. I did not read them, just the first words, which were "No, you can't." Well, I turned on my biological intelligence (which is certainly resting on the lower steps of the universal intelligence ladder - and was in sleep mode) told me this after wake-up was completed: LEGO Lines for DOS is compiled to Intel 8086/8808 machine code. These CPUs do this weird segment/offset addressing - among other modes. The Atari Sixteen/Thirty-two's have a Motorola 68000 CPU under the hood, which has an entirely different instruction set and is using a different addressing model - as it has a linear 32 bit addressing space, among a number of alternative addressing modes. The DOS version uses DOS calls for text/graphics and I/O, the Atari version relies on TOS calls, which are again entirely different. That would result in one hell of work for translation ... I even believe that if we had the source code of TCLogo (maybe in the incarnation of a nice set of C files), we'd need to change a myriad of things to make it compile on a 68000 machine, but who knows! If the OS/CPU line you translate to is of the same type, then yes, I can envision that this executable transfer can happen. Which essentially is what Claude did for you, correct? Well, I should tell Gemini that Claude can do machine code transformation from 8088 to 68000. Or maybe someone here who has a Gemini-Pro++ and Claude-Pro++ account should do that. Maybe we get two AI's clashing with one another ... and Eurobricks will be in the news tomorrow! As far as I am concerned, everything may happen. All the best Thorsten

posts.title: [MOC] Kosmonite's Podracer
posts.text: Built as part of the 2026 Podracing Collab! A lot more pictures and links to the other participants can be found here: https://board.ttvchannel.com/t/kosmonites-podracer-2026-podracer-collab/74183?u=ajtazt ___ One of the rare and unusual living minerals of the galaxy known as the Shards, Kosmonite found himself stranded on Tatooine after a galaxy tour gone wrong. Being the only survivor of the wreck, and of an unknown species to most of the planet, many of its inhabitants assumed he was a droid with an alternative power source and treated him as such. So to earn respect and enough money to get off this horrible planet, he turned to the one thing that wouldn’t immediately turn him away - podracing. After all, although he was a “droid,” he looked like a protocol droid or one of those slow tour pilots. Not something designed to handle the speeds of a podrace, so it would be entertaining to see one try and explode. Yet to everyone’s surprise, Kosmonite and his strange podracer, built from the scraps of an old hyperspace transport ring and the remains of the tour shuttle, survived race after race. And though he earned enough to leave and resume exploring the galaxy, Kosmonite found himself with a new passion. So he choose to continue podracing, traveling to other worlds to try their circuits and racers. ___ Wasn't sure if it was better to post this on the Technic side or Star Wars side, but figured Star Wars was more correct.

posts.title: The Alternative Brick Forum - General Discussion
posts.text: So I built and dismantled my first Lumibricks set, the bodega (when we made the order the barber shop was not in stock, so I have to get that one later and I wanted to get the bodega anyway), and here are some observations: I like the smooth matte finish of the easy to open/close/reuse box. I like the box much more than Lego's boxes. The instructions are super easy to follow and there are very clear instructions how to lay the cables. Easy peasy! Though, like with Lego, it can be hard to distinguish colors in the manual. The finished build looks beautiful, especially when the lights are on (and room lights are dimmed). There are a lot of prints! I think 48 is the number. Print quality though is mixed. The bigger ones at the store front and awning are great but some of the smaller UV-prints maybe lack some sharpness. Generally I prefer pad printing over UV-printing. Clutch power is higher than Lego's and it will make it hard for children to dismantle a build. As a moc builder I prefer Lego's less strong clutch power, which makes it easier to constantly dismantle mocs and use the parts. But I know some people also prefer the higher clutch power. There were two sharp edged tiles without grove and I am pretty sure some people will get hurt when trying to remove these. There was one section where two panels would bend the 1x4 tile that connected both panels. I guess one of the parts was slightly off when it comes to its dimensions. Later, when everything was connected it was not a problem for the build itself. Besides the aformentioned point the parts are of high quality, though for me the look and feel of Lego parts is maybe a tad better in general. Maybe it's the composition of the plastic or whatever. My final verdict is: Integrated lighting makes every set better than a set without lights and if people want a nice building I'd suggest to try out Lumibricks (over Lego Modulars).

That said, the studio sneakily dropping the reported budget 25% after the box office projections lowered is A: scummy and B: evidence that they seem to be expecting failure as well. MoT has pretty much everything riding on it, not least of which Gunn's job. Which is concerning, given the last time that a superman movie's sequel was used as a pseudo justice league movie. You throw in some other things- the purchase meaning the studio is more careful about what they're approving, Supergirl's actress scrubbing all her instagram posts about her role as supergirl, etc- taken seperately none of these things are all that concerning but put together, I may have been right when I said the interval between batman movies could outlast the entire DCU. All it'd take is the Gorilla Grodd show releasing first and that Nightwing/Red Hood street urchins movie rightfully getting cancelled. And of course, by saying that I have now confirmed that the one guy's morbius comparison was an outlier and Clayface is actually going to do so well a sequel is immediately greenlit. You're welcome, DCU fans.
